rationale_summary: The Transparency Chapter of the EU GPAI Code of Practice is predominantly framed around innovation_enablement: across its introductory note, objectives, recitals, and commitments, it emphasizes lowering compliance friction via a user-friendly Model Documentation Form, adhering to proportionality for model modifications, adapting to market and technological developments, promoting trustworthy AI uptake and innovation, and enabling downstream providers to integrate GPAI models into their products. While fundamental_rights and consumer_public_safety appear prominently in the overarching objective imported from Article 1(1) of the AI Act (protecting health, safety, fundamental rights, democracy, and the rule of law against harmful effects of AI), innovation_enablement edges them out because the chapter's specific recitals and operational justifications consistently center on proportionate compliance, value-chain integration, and facilitating trustworthy AI adoption rather than rights or physical-harm discourse. Economic_competitiveness is only weakly present through a single reference to improving the functioning of the internal market.

evidence_spans.quote: To facilitate compliance and fulfilment of the commitments contained in Measure 1.1, we include a user-friendly Model Documentation Form which allows Signatories to easily compile the information required by the aforementioned provisions of the AI Act in a single place.
